transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.
Next I'll compare per-service span counts, error rates and latency between the normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Abnormal latency jumps in ts-food-service, ts-route-plan-service and ts-travel-plan-service, and several services (preserve, payment, security, assurance) have no spans at all. Next I'll check logs and restart/uptime metrics.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, level, count(*) n, min(message) ex FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, level, count(*), min(message) FROM normal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, round(min(value),2) mn, round(max(value),2) mx, round(avg(value),2) av FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.content: {"error": "Result exceeds token budget", "estimated_tokens": 6801, "token_limit": 5000, "suggestions": ["Reduce the LIMIT value", "Filter rows with WHERE clauses to reduce result size", "Use aggregation (COUNT, SUM, AVG) instead of retrieving raw rows"]}

content.text: The only restarts in the abnormal period are three on ts-ticket-office-service. I'll check its uptime and the log distribution, aggregated so the output stays small.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, count(*) n, min(message) ex FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, min(time) t0, max(time) t1, count(*) n, round(min(value),1) mn, round(max(value),1) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.pod.uptime' AND attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE '%ticket%' GROUP BY 1,2,3

content.text: Several services log SEVERE errors (travel-service, route-plan, food, travel-plan). To see which calls drive the latency, I'll pull the normal stats for the services cut off earlier and the caller→callee pairs.

input.query: SELECT 'norm' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,2) p90, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) e5 FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name >= 'ts-station-food' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'ab', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name >= 'ts-station-food' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: ts-travel-service server spans fail with 5xx (2528 of 2660) in a fast, exception-like pattern, and the slowness sits in food, route-plan and travel-plan. To see who calls whom, I'll join client and server spans by parent span.

input.query: SELECT p.service_name caller, c.service_name callee, c.attr_k8s_pod_name callee_pod, count(*) n, round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1) caller_client_ms, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) callee_server_ms, sum(CASE WHEN c.attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) callee_5xx FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id = p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT p.service_name caller, c.service_name callee, c.attr_k8s_pod_name callee_pod, count(*) n, round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1) caller_client_ms, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) callee_server_ms, sum(CASE WHEN c.attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) callee_5xx FROM normal_traces p JOIN normal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id = p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: The call graph points at ts-travel-service: its server spans fail fast with 5xx, and food-service, route-plan-service and travel-plan-service all sit above it. I'll check which span names fail, the exception text, and whether ticket-office appears anywhere outside its restarts.

input.query: SELECT service_name, attr_span_kind, span_name, attr_http_request_method m, attr_http_response_status_code sc, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,1) ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('ts-travel-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-food-service') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2,3 LIMIT 60

SELECT 'log' src, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE '%ticket%' OR message LIKE '%ticket-office%' UNION ALL SELECT 'trace', count(*) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE '%ticket%' OR service_name LIKE '%ticket%' UNION ALL SELECT 'sum', count(*) FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_source LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%ticket%'

content.text: The failure is narrow: only `GET /api/v1/travelservice/routes/{tripId}` fails in ts-travel-service, with fast 500s and an IllegalArgumentException. Route-plan's client calls to travel still take seconds, so I'll check the per-connection hubble metrics and the ticket-office traffic.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),1) av, round(max(value),1) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' AND (attr_source LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_source LIKE '%travel%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%travel%') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),1), round(max(value),1) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' AND (attr_source LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_source LIKE '%travel%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%travel%') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,4,2,1
SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(DISTINCT attr_source) srcs FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The drop counters look like background noise (similar in both periods), and the metric rows have empty service_name, so I'll key on pod names. Next I'll check which user-facing requests at ui-dashboard are affected and what the traces containing the travel failures look like.

input.query: WITH bad AS (SELECT DISTINCT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-travel-service' AND attr_http_response_status_code>=500) SELECT t.service_name, t.attr_span_kind, t.span_name, count(*) n, round(avg(t.duration)/1e6,1) ms, sum(CASE WHEN t.trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM bad) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) in_bad_traces FROM abnormal_traces t WHERE t.attr_span_kind='Server' AND t.service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' OR t.trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM bad) AND t.attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,3 LIMIT 60

SELECT 'norm' p, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, count(*) n, min(value) mn, max(value) mx FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') AND attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-ticket%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'ab', attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, count(*), min(value), max(value) FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') AND attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-ticket%' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: The ticket-office restarts are the same (3) in both periods, so they are baseline and not a fault. Last, I'll compare normal vs abnormal log levels to rule out other faults, and check when the travel 500s start.

input.query: SELECT 'norm' p, service_name, level, count(*) n FROM normal_logs WHERE level IN ('WARN','ERROR','SEVERE') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'ab', service_name, level, count(*) FROM abnormal_logs WHERE level IN ('WARN','ERROR','SEVERE') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 MINUTE, time) AS minute, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-travel-service' AND attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) travel_5xx, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-travel-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) travel_srv, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-route-plan-service' AND attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rp_5xx, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-food-service' AND attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) food_5xx FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The log comparison supports a single fault: the travel-service SEVERE errors (2528) are new, and nothing else changed materially. One more query will confirm that the travel-plan and route-plan failures appear in the same traces as ui-dashboard requests, so the propagation edges are backed.

input.query: SELECT u.service_name AS user_facing, b.service_name AS downstream, b.span_name, count(DISTINCT u.trace_id) traces, round(avg(u.duration)/1e6,1) ui_ms_avg, sum(CASE WHEN b.attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) downstream_5xx FROM abnormal_traces u JOIN abnormal_traces b ON b.trace_id=u.trace_id WHERE u.service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND u.attr_span_kind='Server' AND b.attr_span_kind='Server' AND b.service_name IN ('ts-travel-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-food-service') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2
